## Summary

I implemented the solution in `kindergarten_garden.go` (the only file changed — the test file was left untouched, and no new files were needed):

- **`Garden` type** — holds a per-instance `map[string][]string` of child → plants, so gardens are fully self-contained (satisfies `TestTwoGardens`, which checks that two gardens over the same diagram don't share state).
- **`NewGarden`** — validates the diagram and children, then builds the plant map:
  - Diagram must start with `\n` and contain exactly two rows (catches "wrong diagram format").
  - Rows must be equal length ("mismatched rows") and contain an even number of cups ("odd number of cups").
  - Every cup must be one of `G`/`C`/`R`/`V` → "grass", "clover", "radishes", "violets" (catches "invalid cup codes").
  - Rejects duplicate child names.
  - Copies the `children` slice before sorting, so the caller's argument is never mutated (satisfies `TestNamesNotModified`).
  - Assigns each alphabetically-sorted child two cups per row (columns `2i`, `2i+1`), producing the four-plant list in the order: row 1 left→right, then row 2 left→right.
- **`Plants`** — map lookup returning `([]string, bool)`, with `ok = false` for children not in the garden.

Test run: all 15 subtests pass (`TestGarden` with 12 subtests, `TestNamesNotModified`, `TestTwoGardens`).
